info.title: sap-for-agents — SAP NWRFC → REST gateway
info.description: Expose SAP RFC/BAPI function modules as HTTP endpoints. Any language or AI agent that can POST JSON can call SAP through this gateway, without installing an SAP client or NWRFC SDK. Machine-readable contract for AI self-service: search → inspect interface → read docs → invoke.

tags.name: discovery
tags.description: AI-facing metadata endpoints (search / interface / docs / DDIC)

tags.name: objects
tags.description: ABAP object writes (lock → write → unlock → activate orchestrated)

tags.name: adt
tags.description: ADT REST proxy (Eclipse tooling API pass-through)

tags.name: registry
tags.description: API registry — cross-session memory of agent-built interfaces (gateway-local, survives restarts)

get.summary: Readiness probe (pings SAP via RFC_PING, 5s timeout)
get.description: Verifies SAP reachability through the connection pool. Returns 503 when SAP is unreachable or times out — orchestrators should remove this instance from load balancing, not restart it.

get.summary: Prometheus metrics (connection pool + RFC call counters/latency)

get.description: Human/AI-readable guide for using this gateway. Start here if you don't know which endpoint fits your task.

get.summary: Gateway version + capability self-description (public, does not fail on SAP outage)
get.description: Gateway version/git commit, capability switches (auth, read_only, adt, rate_limit_rps) and SAP system info (sysid, release, host, os, client). Call this first in a new session instead of probing 401/403/503/429 by trial. SAP info is fetched lazily on first call and cached for the process lifetime; when SAP is unreachable, `sap` is null and `sap_error` carries the reason (still HTTP 200).

200.description: Version and capabilities (sap block may be null)

get.description: v0.16: the gateway can connect to several SAP systems at once (sap_systems.toml). This endpoint lists them — name, whether default, read_only, adt enabled, sysid (once connected), quarantined. Every /api/* endpoint also has a scoped form: /api/s/{system}/... (e.g. POST /api/s/prd/rfc) targets that system; unprefixed paths hit the default. Single-system deployments list one entry.

v0.17: first-run onboarding for agents. When the gateway starts with no sap_systems.toml and no SAP_* connection env vars, it still listens (unconfigured mode): business endpoints return 503 SYSTEM_NOT_CONFIGURED and this endpoint tells an agent how to proceed — whether a config is in place, where the config file lives, whether setup writes are allowed (SAP_SETUP=off disables), and a `fields` checklist (name/ashost/sysnr/client/user/passwd/...) to interview the user with. POST /api/setup/system then validates, optionally test-connects, persists sap_systems.toml and hot-loads the system without a restart.

post.summary: Add an SAP system (guided setup: validate → test-connect → persist → hot-load)
post.description: v0.17: agent-guided configuration write. Body fields mirror one [systems.{name}] table of sap_systems.toml (unknown keys are rejected). Flow: build_spec validation (same rules as startup parsing, incl. ${VAR} interpolation) → real test connection (RFC open + system info; skipped with `test:false`) → SYSID conflict check → persist to sap_systems.toml (existing entries preserved; env-synthesized default system persisted on first write) → hot-load into the running gateway. The first system always becomes the default. 400 SETUP_PARAM_INVALID / 409 SETUP_NAME_EXISTS or SYSTEM_SYSID_CONFLICT / 403 SETUP_DISABLED (SAP_SETUP=off) / 502 SETUP_CONNECT_FAILED (nothing persisted).

ashost.description: Application server host (direct form; or use conn.MSHOST for load balancing)

sysnr.description: System number (two digits, e.g. 00) — required with ashost

default.description: Make this the default system (the first system always becomes default)

test.description: Test-connect before persisting (default true; false = offline pre-provisioning, unverified)

conn.description: Free-form SDK connection params (upper-cased, passed through): MSHOST/R3NAME/GROUP for load-balanced connections

200.description: Saved + hot-loaded (connection block carries sysid/release when tested)

post.summary: Reload a system's runtime state (pool generation + metadata cache)
post.description: v0.18: makes a system behave as if the gateway had just been restarted — without restarting the process. The listener stays up and in-flight requests finish on their old connection. Two caches go stale when an SAP-side RFC interface changes (parameters added/removed/retyped): the SDK's per-connection function-descriptor cache and the gateway's per-function metadata cache. This endpoint bumps the connection-pool generation (idle connections closed immediately, borrowed ones dropped on return) and clears the function/DDIC metadata cache, so the next call reconnects and re-reads the signature from SAP. Call it after changing an RFC in SE37/SE80 and before trusting /api/functions or /api/rfc. Scoped form: POST /api/s/{system}/admin/reload. It does NOT re-read .env or sap_systems.toml — config changes still need a process restart (adding systems hot-loads via POST /api/setup/system). Safe on read_only systems: it only resets local caches.

post.summary: Gracefully restart the gateway process (drain then exit)
post.description: v0.18: the only correct way to apply changes that live outside a system's runtime state — .env values (SAP_API_KEY, SAP_LISTEN_ADDR, SAP_POOL_SIZE, SAP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS) or a different binary. Returns 202 immediately; the restart happens asynchronously. Sequence: /ready starts returning 503 with Retry-After for SAP_DRAIN_SECS seconds (default 5) while the listener keeps serving in-flight requests, then the process exits with code 0. The process only comes back if a supervisor restarts it (`start.sh` guard loop, launchd KeepAlive, systemd Restart=always, docker --restart). Started as a bare exec, it stays down — check the `warning` field in the response. For RFC signature changes use POST /api/admin/reload instead: it needs no restart and keeps the listener up. Scoped form: POST /api/s/{system}/admin/restart (the system segment is ignored — restart is process-wide).

202.description: Accepted: status=restarting, drain_secs, warning about supervisor requirement

post.summary: Invoke any SAP RFC/BAPI function module
post.description: Generic invocation: fill `func_name` plus the parameters you care about; outputs you request are returned as JSON. For write BAPIs (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE) you must call BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT afterwards or the changes won't take effect. Check the RETURN table (read_return: true) for TYPE=E rows instead of relying on HTTP status.

200.description: Function executed (may still carry SAP-side errors in return_table)

post.description: `*` matches anything, e.g. `BAPI_USER_*`, `RFC_*`. Returns 200 with an empty list when nothing matches (not an error). At least one of pattern / group must be non-empty.

get.description: Returns parameter names (case-sensitive, always UPPERCASE), types (CHAR/INT/TABLE/...), directions (IMPORT/EXPORT/TABLES), lengths and nested fields. Inspect this before invoking to avoid 90% of parameter mistakes.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Function module name, e.g. BAPI_USER_GETLIST. Namespaced names (containing /) are supported via the raw or percent-encoded form.

get.description: Returns short_text, long_text (full SE37 documentation, may be empty) and per-parameter docs. Empty long_text is normal — read parameter_docs instead.

parameters.name: lang
parameters.description: Documentation language (e.g. EN, DE, ZH). Defaults to SAP_LANG env.

get.summary: Read a function module's ABAP source
get.description: Reads via RPY_FUNCTIONMODULE_READ; on non-404 failures it falls back to the ADT channel automatically (response `source_via` tells you which path served the lines: "rfc" or "adt"). `?prologue=true` appends a `prologue` section: signatures of the function's CALL FUNCTION dependencies.
Reads via RPY_PROGRAM_READ; falls back to the ADT channel on failure. The `source_via` field tells which path served the lines ("rfc" or "adt").
Widely available for structures (e.g. BAPIRET2); for transparent tables (e.g. MARA) it depends on the target system's DDIC configuration — some systems return NOT_FOUND.

get.summary: Inspect a field's semantics (data element / domain / fixed values)
get.description: Especially useful for status-code / type fields: fixed_values tells you which values are legal.

post.summary: Read transparent table data (no RFC_READ_TABLE plumbing)
post.description: Wraps RFC_READ_TABLE with ET_DATA (avoids the 512-byte truncation). rowcount defaults to 1000, max 10000. WHERE clauses are ABAP Open SQL fragments, one per array element.

get.description: Every remote-enabled function module successfully written through this gateway is auto-registered here as a draft entry; entries carry intent / pitfalls / example invocations and survive restarts. Check this first in a new session before searching SAP. Tombstoned entries (their FM was deleted) are hidden unless include_deleted=true.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring filter on alias / func_name / intent (case-insensitive)

put.description: PUT is a FULL replace (GET first, merge, PUT back). Auto-registered drafts keep their origin. status accepts draft/published only (deletion goes through DELETE).

delete.summary: Tombstone (default) or physically remove an entry

parameters.name: purge
parameters.description: true = physical removal (default tombstones for the record)

get.summary: Recent invoke audit trail (last ~500, newest first)
get.description: Ring buffer of the most recent calls across /api/rfc, typed invokes and flat invokes: timestamp, source endpoint (via), registry alias when applicable, function name, ok/status, duration in ms, caller IP. For quick troubleshooting without log access.

post.summary: Flat invoke of a registered API (consumer-facing delivery port)
post.description: Flat JSON in / flat JSON out — no SAP dialect needed. The contract is derived from the function's live interface metadata: input keys map to parameters (case-insensitive; structures are objects, tables are arrays of row objects), all outputs are returned by true type, output tables are row-capped (?limit= overrides; default 100, entry max_rows overrides the default). Response carries "_truncated" listing capped tables when truncation occurred. Unknown body keys are rejected with 400 (allowed keys listed). Alias comes from GET /api/registry; published entries also appear as fully typed operations in this spec.

200.description: Flat result: output parameter name → value

get.summary: Structured short-dump list (parsed from the ADT Atom feed)
get.description: ST22 entries newest-first, parsed into structured items (no 45KB–1MB raw text). Each item's `key` plugs into /api/dumps/{key}/detail.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start time, UTC yyyyMMddHHmmss (server-side paging in ADT)

get.summary: Dumps grouped by (error type, terminated program)
get.description: Answers "what keeps failing". Groups sorted by count desc; `latest_key` plugs straight into the detail endpoint.

get.summary: One dump's structured detail (header / termination point / call stack)
get.description: Take `key` from the list endpoint's items. Raw %20-encoded or decoded keys both work. Note: OpenAPI cannot express a multi-segment path parameter — {key} may contain slashes.

get.summary: Read an object's source (ADT channel, original casing)
get.description: type ∈ prog|incl|class|intf|func|fugr|cds|tabl (package has no source; tabl returns the DDIC table DDL 'define table ...' form; stru the structure DDL 'define structure ...'). For func the group is auto-resolved when not given. Returns lines[] plus the joined source string.

put.summary: Write an object's full source (lock → put → unlock → activate, orchestrated)
put.description: type ∈ prog|incl|class|intf|func|fugr|cds|tabl (tabl/stru = DDIC table/structure DDL sources, written lock-free with etag optimistic concurrency); name may contain / (namespaced objects, e.g. /UI5/CL_X — OpenAPI cannot express multi-segment path params). Activation failure is a logical result (HTTP 200 + activated.messages), not a transport error. For func objects the function group is auto-resolved when not given; FM parameter signatures are part of the source (inline in the FUNCTION statement; classic *" comment blocks are converted automatically); rfc_enabled:true additionally marks the module remote-enabled.

post.description: Reads the current source, replaces `old_string` with `new_string` (must match exactly once and change the content), then runs the same write orchestration as PUT /source.
Submits the given source for a syntax check (nothing is persisted).

post.summary: Create an object shell (ADT-first; prog/func fall back to RFC)
post.description: type ∈ prog|incl|class|intf|func|fugr|cds|tabl|stru|package. Creates the object via the standard ADT objectcreation XML (Eclipse/vsp/abapfs contract); prog/func fall back to the RFC RPY insert path when ADT fails. func auto-creates its function group when missing. package: devclass = parent package, software_component optional (candidates ZLOCAL→LOCAL→HOME). Optional `source` writes+activates the first version in one call; rfc_enabled marks a func remote-enabled.

description.description: Object title / short text (required by SAP)

devclass.description: Package (default $TMP); for package type: parent package

source.description: Optional first source (written + activated in one call)

rfc_enabled.description: func only: mark remote-enabled after the first write

delete.description: type ∈ prog|incl|class|intf|func|fugr|cds|tabl|stru|package. Deleting a fugr removes its function modules too. Query params: group (func only), transport. Irreversible.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Function group (func only; auto-resolved when omitted)

get.description: Transparently proxies the SAP system's ADT REST API (/sap/bc/adt/** on ICF — the same API Eclipse uses). The URL after /api/adt/ maps 1:1 to the ADT path; Accept/Content-Type/If-Match headers and body are forwarded, responses passed through verbatim (mostly XML). Write methods get X-CSRF-Token + session handling automatically (retries once on 403). Gateway-side failures use the JSON error contract (400 ADT_PATH_INVALID / 502 ADT_UNREACHABLE / 503 ADT_DISABLED / 504 ADT_TIMEOUT); other statuses come from ADT itself. Note: OpenAPI cannot express a multi-segment path parameter — {path} here may contain slashes (e.g. runtime/dumps).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: ADT sub-path, e.g. runtime/dumps or oo/classes/CL_RUNTIME_ERROR/source/main

version.description: Gateway version (same as /api/version, convenience for pollers)

commit.description: Git short commit the binary was built from; '-dirty' suffix when the working tree had uncommitted changes, 'unknown' when built without git

capabilities.description: Deployment switches that change agent behavior

auth.description: true = SAP_API_KEY is set; /api/* requires Bearer token (this endpoint excepted)

read_only.description: true = SAP_READ_ONLY; gateway write endpoints return 403 READ_ONLY

latest.description: Latest GitHub release, from a background check (startup + every 24h, one anonymous GET — disable with SAP_UPDATE_CHECK=off). null when not fetched / disabled / unreachable; never blocks the response

update_available.description: true = the running version is older than this release

sap.description: Target SAP system info, cached from the first successful fetch; null when SAP is currently unreachable

release.description: SAP release (RFCSI SAPRL, e.g. 753/816). Reflects the kernel/Basis level only — to distinguish ECC vs S/4HANA, check the CVERS table for the S4CORE component (POST /api/table/read)

sap_error.description: Present when sap is null: why the SAP info fetch failed (retryable on next call)

ScalarValue.description: Scalar parameter value. Implicit dispatch by JSON type: string → CHAR/NUM/DATE/TIME/BCD-as-string, integer → INT, float → FLOAT. Explicit type markers for BCD/INT8/binary: {"type":"BCD","value":"123.45"}, {"type":"INT8","value":123}, {"type":"BYTES","value":"<base64>"}.

value.description: BCD → numeric string; INT8 → integer; BYTES → Base64 string

MaxLen.description: String-output max length. Legacy form: plain integer. Detailed form: {"max_len": 255} (null = auto-discover from metadata).

auto.description: true = read by the field's true DDIC type (INT→integer, FLOAT→float, INT8→i64, BYTE/XSTRING→Base64), false (default) = string

func_name.description: RFC function module name, UPPERCASE, e.g. BAPI_USER_GETLIST. Max 30 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_], optional /NS/ namespace prefix.

table_inputs.description: TABLES input parameters: name → array of rows; each row is {field: value}. Max 100000 rows per table.

struct_inputs.description: Top-level IMPORTING structure parameters: name → {field: value}, e.g. BAPI_USER_CREATE.ADDRESS

int_outputs.description: EXPORT integer parameter names to read

string_outputs.description: EXPORT string parameter names to read → max length. A STRUCTURE-typed parameter is read into structs by its sub-fields automatically.

auto_outputs.description: EXPORT scalar parameter names to read by their true metadata type (INT→integer, FLOAT→float, INT8→i64, BCD→string, BYTE/XSTRING→Base64)

table_outputs.description: EXPORT/TABLES tables to traverse: name → field list. Output rows are capped at 10000 (use /api/table/read for pagination).

struct_outputs.description: Top-level structure outputs: name → field list (same rules as table_outputs)

read_return.description: Automatically read the BAPI RETURN message table (rows with TYPE=E indicate errors)

timeout_secs.description: Per-call timeout in seconds. Omit to use the global default (60s); relax it for slow endpoints (batch BAPIs, large tables). 504 on timeout.

scalars.description: Scalar outputs; value type depends on the read method

tables.description: Table outputs: name → array of rows ({field: value}); auto:true fields keep native types, others are strings

structs.description: Top-level structure outputs (same value-type rules as tables)

return_table.description: RETURN messages (when read_return=true and the table exists). TYPE=E rows are errors.

pattern.description: Function name wildcard, * matches anything, e.g. BAPI_USER_*

name.description: Use this exact UPPERCASE name when invoking

interface_via.description: Which channel served the interface: fii = live server-side read (always fresh, default), sdk = SDK descriptor cache (fallback when FII is unavailable)

long_text.description: Full SE37 documentation; may be empty (normal)

warning.description: Present when documentation could not be read

source_via.description: Which channel served the lines: rfc (RPY_*_READ) or adt (fallback after RPY failure)

prologue.description: Only with /api/functions/{name}/source?prologue=true: signatures of the function's CALL FUNCTION dependencies

table.description: Transparent table name, e.g. T000, USR01

fields.description: Fields to select (determines column order and field-name mapping)

where.description: WHERE conditions (ABAP Open SQL fragments, one per element; empty = no filter)

delimiter.description: Field delimiter for parsing (default \u0001; change only if values contain it)

alias.description: Unique lowercase URL-safe id (team/name prefixes allowed)

intent.description: What this API is for, who consumes it (agent-written)

doc.description: Consumer-facing Markdown documentation; rendered in the OpenAPI catalog's operation description

status.description: deleted = tombstone (FM was deleted; record kept)

origin.description: auto = created by the write hook on rfc_enabled FM writes

intent.description: What this API is for (default empty)

items.description: Field name → value (all values are strings)

transport.description: Transport request number; omitted = reuse the object's bound request

group.description: Function group (func objects only); omitted = auto-resolved via RFC_FUNCTION_SEARCH

rfc_enabled.description: func only: mark the function module remote-enabled (processingType=rfc) under the same lock

old_string.description: Must match exactly once in the current source

rfc_enabled.description: func only: mark remote-enabled after the write

source_url.description: ADT source URL of the object

key.description: Machine-readable code, e.g. FU_NOT_FOUND / AUTH_INVALID / RATE_LIMITED / JSON_INVALID

Error.description: Error (4xx = caller-side, 5xx = SAP/network). Branch on error.code (HTTP status) and error.key (machine code).
